summary: Role switch to engineering service account fails after org rename — 403 denied due to missing delegated_groups claim
description:
Issue summary:
Users can no longer 'Switch role' to the engineering service account in Internal-Ops after a recent Okta org rename (org slug changed). Attempts to assume the role return 403 Forbidden with an auth error indicating a missing delegated_groups claim in the inbound OIDC assertion.

Impact:
- Internal SRE and oncall engineers are unable to escalate or run 'impersonate' operations through Internal-Ops tooling for ~25 users in the Eng org.
- Workflows requiring delegated service-account access (deploys, incident runbooks) are blocked for affected users. No customer-facing outage reported, but incident response is slowed.

Environment:
prod (us-east). Affected users appear limited to accounts that were migrated during the org rename.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Login to Internal-Ops via Okta SSO as a migrated user.
2) Open the 'Switch role' modal and select 'engineering-service-account'.
3) Click 'Assume role' -> Immediately receive 403 Forbidden with trace id shown in console.

Observed logs/response:
- Identity-proxy logs: "auth_error: missing claim 'delegated_groups' in token" (trace: 8a1b2c3d)
- Internal-Ops frontend: 403 response from /api/v1/assume-role, body: "insufficient_scopes"
- Okta SCIM logs show successful user profile update during org rename but group membership attribute used by the claim mapping looks like it retained old org slug values.

Temporary workaround:
Team lead used an admin backdoor (console-level impersonation) to perform one-off tasks while we investigate. Not scalable.
investigation_notes: 03/10 10:45 - Confirmed error reproduces for migrated users; non-migrated users can switch roles successfully.

03/10 12:10 - Pulled identity-proxy token decoding: delegated_groups claim absent in token for migrated user; groups present in Okta profile but claim mapping appears to filter by /orgs/{slug}/ prefix.

03/10 14:00 - SCIM provisioning job (sync-org-rename-v2) ran during migration; review shows group names were rewritten (org-slug-old -> org-slug-new) but claim mapping config still expecting old prefix.
03/11 09:30 - Cross-referenced with INT-202406 (group-encoding-mismatch) which had similar symptoms; likely related but not identical due to rename metadata.
03/11 11:00 - Small PR prepared to relax prefix matching in claim-mapper (identity-proxy) while preserving security checks (see PR 482).
comments: Aisha Patel (reporter) 2026-03-10 10:40: "Started seeing multiple SREs report 403 when switching to service-account after org rename. Collected sample trace ids and attached logs."
Ethan Novak (assignee) 2026-03-10 11:05: "Acknowledged. I'll validate tokens and claim mappings. Assigning SRE to reproduce and collect token jwk/headers."

Samira Chen (SRE) 2026-03-10 12:20: "Reproduced locally: token from Okta lacks delegated_groups even though 'groups' in profile present. SCIM migration may have rewritten group names; need to verify claim-mapper config."

Diego Ramos (Identity) 2026-03-11 09:45: "Okta mapping uses attribute expression `groups[startsWith('/orgs/old-slug/')]`. Org rename left some legacy group names with old-slug due to delayed rename job; will sync and consider mapping change."
Ethan Novak 2026-03-11 15:30: "Opening hotfix PR to adjust claim-mapper to accept either old-slug or new-slug while we reconcile SCIM data. Will run canary against a small user subset."
resolution: Work in progress: hotfix PR opened to identity-proxy (relaxed prefix match with allowlist) and canary rollout scheduled. Next steps: run reconciliation job to normalize group names across SCIM, deploy PR to staging and canary in prod for subset, monitor role-switch success metrics, then promote. Post-mortem and follow-up task to update org-rename runbook to include claim-mapping verification.
